subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Green <alex@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance

Alex / Sophie — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to keep things moving. Please reply if I missed or misstated anything.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Bursty production traffic during month-end reporting causing token-level cost spikes and occasional throttling in your hosted endpoints.
- Need for predictable TPS and consistent tail latency for customer-facing summarization features.
- Data isolation and stronger controls for PII/financial data (audit logs, KMS integration).

Current stack you described:
- Inference calls served today via a managed endpoint (third-party) running a fine-tuned open model.
- Preprocessing in Python microservices on GCP, request routing through an API Gateway.
- No current on-prem infra; willing to evaluate VPC/private deployments or Redwood Dedicated reserved pools.

Key success criteria you mentioned:
1) Predictable throughput of 200 reqs/s sustained with spikes to 800 reqs/s for short periods (1-2 hours).
2) 95th percentile latency under 300ms for short prompts (<512 tokens).
3) Dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation and customer-managed key usage (KMS).
4) Autoscaling/burst policy that guarantees capacity for business-critical windows (month-end).

Suggested fit: Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) looks like a strong candidate given the isolation and predictable TPS requirements. We can map a GPU pool (mix of GPU instances) with burst capacity + canaries for rollouts.

Open questions / info we need from you to scope a proposal:
- Typical and peak tokens/sec (or requests/sec) by hour (if you can share the spreadsheet you mentioned that would help).
- Expected production go-live target (quarter/date).
- Any compliance artifacts we should prep early (SOC 2, encryption standards, IP allowlists).

Next steps:
- Action: Alex to send throughput spreadsheet (requested)  - target: today.
- Action: Rafael to circulate a short SOW stub and proposed hardware profile for initial sizing (attached).
- Action: Schedule SE technical deep-dive next week to validate kv-cache strategy, batching and quantization options (please propose 2x slots).

Attachments: Aurora_Dedicated_SOW_stub.pdf (draft), Redwood sizing checklist (inline).

Thanks - Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Green <alex@aurorafinance.com>

Cc: Sophie Li <sophie.li@aurorafinance.com>, procurement@aurorafinance.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications and I attached the throughput estimates spreadsheet as discussed.

Clarifications:
- Our sustained baseline is ~180-220 reqs/s during business hours; month-end windows push sustained to ~600-800 reqs/s for 1-3 hour blocks.
- Typical prompt sizes are 200-600 tokens; Summarization and entity-extraction workloads dominate.
- Encryption: we must use customer-managed KMS for keys and have audit logs retained for 2 years.

Attached: Aurora_throughput_estimates.xlsx (hourly RPS and token distribution).

We can target a soft go-live by mid-Q4, but procurement may need an end-of-July contract target to align budgets.

- Alex Green
Head of ML Platforms | Aurora Finance
alex@aurorafinance.com | +1 (646) 555-0199

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Green <alex@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Li <sophie.li@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap — Aurora Finance

Appreciate the spreadsheet, Alex - that helps a lot. Looping in Marissa (Sales Engineer) and Lauren (AM) to schedule the technical deep-dive and to start sizing the Dedicated pool and burst policy.

Marissa - can you review the attached throughput sheet and propose an initial hardware profile (GPU types, number of slots) and an autoscaling/burst policy that meets their 600-800 reqs/s spikes while keeping steady-state cost-efficient? Some constraints to bake in: 1) KMS integration, 2) audit log retention 2 years, 3) ability to pin model versions per environment.

Proposed SE deep-dive agenda (45-60m):
- Walk through request/response characteristics and KV cache opportunities (10m)
- Sizing: batch sizes, typical sequence lengths, expected token/sec (15m)
- Autoscaling/burst policy options and SLA targets (15m)
- Security/compliance ask-list and next steps (5-10m)

Alex/Sophie - can you share 2x 1-hour slots next week (we have availability Tue 6/15 10-12 PT and Wed 6/16 14-16 PT).

Rafael

Thanks Rafael. A couple of security/compliance items for the deep-dive so we can validate fit on our side:

1) SOC 2 Type II report and recent penetration test (can you send redacted copies or a secure link?).
2) KMS options - we need confirmation you support AWS KMS and bring-your-own-key for private deployments.
3) Audit logging: event retention, export formats, and whether logs can be shipped to our SIEM (we use Splunk).
4) Data retention & deletion policy for request/response logs (we need the ability to opt-out of storing PII).

Also requesting an initial cost estimate range tied to the sizing proposal (ballpark $/month for baseline + burst allocation) so procurement can preliminarily assess budget.

We can take Tue 6/15 10:30-11:30 PT for the technical session. Procurement will be on the call.

Sophie Li
